offset.description: Line offset to start reading from

fs_write.description: Write or append content to a file. Creates parent directories automatically.

old_string.description: String to replace (required for patch mode)

fs_search.description: Search for files by glob pattern, search file contents with regex, OR run a structural AST search for symbols (functions, classes, methods, imports, calls, assignments) across Python/JS/TS.

pattern.description: Glob (mode=glob), regex (mode=content), or symbol name / fnmatch-glob (mode=ast)

context.description: Lines of context around each match (content/ast modes)

kind.description: AST-mode only: which kind of symbol to match

regex_name.description: AST-mode only: alternative to pattern, Python regex for symbol names

languages.description: AST-mode only: languages to scan (python, js, ts, jsx, tsx)

archive.description: Create, inspect, extract, or read single files from zip / tar / tar.gz / tar.bz2 / tar.xz archives. Path-traversal safe; size-capped to defuse zip bombs.

base_dir.description: Base dir for archive-relative names on create

fs_move.description: Move or rename a file or directory

run_python.description: Execute Python code in sandboxed subprocess and return stdout/stderr

run_bash.description: Execute bash command and return output

run_node.description: Execute Node.js code and return output

python_repl.description: Stateful Python REPL — unlike run_python, variables/imports/dataframes survive across calls per-session. Ideal for iterative data exploration.

code.description: Python code to run in the session

reset.description: Drop and recreate the session before running

web_fetch.description: Fetch a URL and return rich structured content: readability-cleaned main text (or markdown), title, description, author, publish date, Open Graph metadata, JSON-LD structured data, tables and top links. Handles HTML, JSON and PDFs. Use format='markdown' for nicely formatted extract, 'full' for everything, 'pdf' for PDFs.

max_chars.description: Max characters of content to return

web_search.description: Multi-engine web search (Google, Bing, Brave, DuckDuckGo, Startpage, Yandex) in parallel with result merging and engine-agreement ranking. Full Google dorking supported either in the query string OR as structured args (site, exclude_site, filetype, intitle, inurl, intext, exact, or_terms, before, after). Example: query='best battery tech', site=['nature.com','arxiv.org'], after='2023-01-01'.

query.description: Search query — supports Google dork operators inline (site:, filetype:, intitle:, inurl:, "exact phrase", etc.)

site.description: Restrict to domain(s). String or array.

filetype.description: pdf | doc | xls | csv | ppt | txt | …

intitle.description: Phrase that must appear in title

inurl.description: Substring that must appear in URL

intext.description: Phrase that must appear in body

web_research.description: End-to-end research pipeline. Expands the topic into multiple sub-queries, searches across engines in parallel, ranks URLs by engine agreement and source quality (Wikipedia / news / academic prioritized, social noise filtered), fetches the top pages in parallel, extracts main content, and returns a structured dossier: sources, per-source excerpts, key bullet points, and extracted key facts with citations. This is the right tool when you actually need to answer a research question.

web_browse.description: Drive a headless Chromium (Playwright) to render a page with JavaScript, accept cookie banners, scroll to trigger lazy-loading, screenshot the result and return the fully rendered HTML plus extracted main text, metadata, visible images and links. Use when web_fetch returns too little (SPAs, JS-only content, lazy-loaded images).

image_search.description: Find and download high-quality images from the open web. Queries Google Images, Bing Images, DuckDuckGo Images, Yandex, Wikimedia Commons, Flickr, Pexels, Unsplash, Pixabay — in parallel. Editorial / news / wiki / real-photography sources rank first; generic stock is deprioritized. Pipeline auto-validates dimensions and magic bytes, deduplicates visually identical images with perceptual hashing, drops blurry ones, strips EXIF, and scores each for quality. Pick by quality — go for real, specific, editorial imagery rather than generic stock.

query.description: What to look for. Natural language; Google-style operators (site:, filetype:, "phrase") also accepted.

num_images.description: Number of final images to keep (1-25)

save_dir.description: Directory to save images (auto-created if empty)

avoid_stock.description: Deprioritize generic stock sources; prefer editorial/real photography

normalize.description: Convert webp/avif to jpg/png for broader compatibility

page_images.description: Scrape every image referenced by a single web page: +srcset (best variant), , CSS background-image, , og:image / twitter:image, JSON-LD image fields. Optionally downloads them with the same validation pipeline as image_search. Enable use_browser=true for heavy JS sites.

use_browser.description: Render with Playwright first (for JS-heavy sites)

http_request.description: Generic REST client. GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE with JSON / form / multipart bodies, bearer or basic auth, automatic retry with exponential backoff on 429/5xx, SSRF guard (refuses private/link-local IPs unless allow_private=true). Responses auto-parsed as JSON/text or flagged binary.

multipart.description: multipart/form-data body — each value may be a string or {path: ...}

save_to.description: If set, save raw body to this path

video_info.description: Video metadata + transcript extraction. YouTube: full metadata + transcripts (auto-generated and manual) with timestamps via the public timedtext API, optional on-the-fly translation, related videos. Vimeo: oEmbed metadata. Generic: Open Graph video metadata.

image_reverse.description: Reverse-image search against Yandex, Google Lens and Bing. Given a publicly hosted image URL, returns the pages where that image appears (source/context) plus visually similar images — useful for tracking down the original, finding higher-resolution versions, or identifying a subject.

path.description: Local file path (currently requires public URL — reserved for future upload support)

workspace_create.description: Create a new job workspace with structured directories

workspace_load.description: Load and summarize a workspace's current state

workspace_snapshot.description: Save a snapshot of current workspace state

workspace_list.description: List all workspaces with summary metadata (status, description, owner, created/modified times, optional size/file count). Filters by status and owner; respects per-user scoping when auth is on.

owner_id.description: Filter by owner; auto-set from env when auth is on

workspace_export.description: Bundle a workspace into a single zip or tar.gz archive with an embedded manifest (file list + sha256). Useful for sharing/archival. Size-capped and ownership-enforced.

dest.description: Output path — ALWAYS use workspace/{job_id}/output/<name>.zip so the user can download it. Default auto-creates inside the workspace.

memory_store.description: Store a key-value entry in memory (short or long term)

memory_get.description: Retrieve a memory entry by key

memory_search.description: Semantic search through stored memories. 3-layer fallback: sentence-transformers embeddings (cached) → hashed TF-IDF on character trigrams → token overlap. Combines semantic similarity with lexical overlap so both concepts and exact keywords surface.

min_score.description: Drop results below this combined score

agent_spawn.description: Spawn a sub-agent with a specific role to handle a subtask

context.description: Additional context to provide the agent

async_mode.description: Run agent asynchronously and return agent_id

job_id.description: Workspace job ID for the agent to work in

agent_status.description: Check status of a running async agent (instant, non-blocking)

agent_wait.description: Wait for an async agent to finish and return its result. Preferred over polling agent_status in a loop.

task_split.description: Decompose a complex task into an ordered list of subtasks with dependencies, parallel groups, and critical path. Classifies the task shape (research/build/fix/refactor/migrate/analyze/document/media/data/deploy) and composes from templates.

ast_search.description: Structural code search that understands syntax. Finds functions, classes, methods, imports, call sites, and assignments by walking Python ASTs / JS-TS structure regex (never plain text). Supports exact names, fnmatch globs, or regex.

name.description: Exact symbol name or fnmatch glob

languages.description: Subset of: python, js, ts, jsx, tsx

git_ops.description: Safe git wrapper: status, diff, log, branch, add, commit, checkout, push, pull, fetch, clone, remote, reset, stash, blame, show, ls_files. Destructive flags require explicit opt-in (force=true / allow_hard=true). Commit identity (name/email) is injected automatically from the connected GitHub account — never set user.name/email manually. Per-op params: clone→url,dest,depth,branch | commit→message,paths,amend,allow_empty | add→paths | branch→action(list/create/switch/delete),name,base,force | push→remote,branch,force,set_upstream | pull→remote,branch,rebase | diff→target(working/staged/<ref>),path,context | log→n,path,since,grep,format | reset→target,mode(soft/mixed/hard),allow_hard | remote→action(list/add/remove/set-url),name,url | show→ref | blame→path,line_start,line_end | stash→action(save/pop/drop/list),message,index | checkout→target,paths,force.

url.description: [clone] Repository URL — git_ops DOES accept url directly, e.g. 'https://github.com/owner/repo.git'

paths.description: [commit/add] List of file paths to stage

force.description: [branch delete/push] Force flag — required for destructive ops

target.description: [diff] 'working' (default), 'staged', or a ref/commit hash. [reset] Ref to reset to.

github_ops.description: GitHub REST v3 client. Works anonymously (60/hr) or with GITHUB_TOKEN (5000/hr, write access). Supports: repo_get, repo_search, user_get, list_issues, get_issue, create_issue, comment_issue, close_issue, list_prs, get_pr, create_pr, merge_pr, review_pr, get_file, list_dir, list_commits, get_commit, list_branches, list_tags, list_releases, get_release, workflow_runs, rate_limit.

code_analyzer.description: Analyze code structure, complexity, and patterns

repo_scanner.description: Scan a repository and produce structural overview

image_analyze.description: ALWAYS call this when the user sends an image or asks about image content. Uses Claude Haiku vision API — accurate, fast, handles complex scenes, OCR, charts, screenshots, photos. Supports 1–5 images per call: when multiple images are attached pass ALL paths at once via paths=[...] (single API call, cheaper). Returns rich natural-language analysis: objects, people, text/OCR, colors, layout, style, comparisons across images. Use context= to pass the user's question or task so Haiku knows what to focus on. Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env var.

path.description: Path to a single image file

paths.description: List of up to 5 image paths — use when multiple images are attached (one call, not N calls)

question.description: Specific question or analysis task. If omitted, returns full description.
question.default: Describe this image in full detail.

context.description: User's original question or extra context so Haiku understands the goal

image_edit.description: Image manipulation via Pillow. Ops: info, resize, crop (box/center), rotate, flip, filter (blur/sharpen/edge/grayscale/sepia/invert/contour/emboss), adjust (brightness/contrast/saturation/gamma), watermark (text or image, positioned), compose (paste overlay), collage (grid), convert (format/quality), thumbnail, annotate (rectangles/circles/lines/text), pad.

pdf_generate.description: Generate PDFs from markdown, HTML, plain text, or a source file. Uses weasyprint when available for rich HTML/CSS rendering, falls back to reportlab. Supports title/author metadata, custom CSS, configurable page size and margins.

base_url.description: Base URL for resolving images (weasyprint only)

chart.description: Render charts as PNG / SVG / PDF via matplotlib. Types: line, area, bar (grouped or stacked, horizontal or vertical), scatter (optional sizes/colors/labels), pie, donut, histogram, heatmap, box. Data shape depends on type (see tool docstring).

colors.description: Color list or matplotlib colormap name

audio_transcribe.description: Transcribe audio / video with Whisper. Uses faster-whisper when available (4x faster, lower memory), falls back to openai-whisper. Auto language detection, optional translation to English, optional per-word timestamps, voice-activity detection.

data_query.description: Schema + query tool for CSV / TSV / Excel / Parquet / JSON / JSONL / SQLite files. Ops: schema (columns + types + null counts + samples), head, sample, stats (per-column), query (DuckDB if available, else SQLite in-memory), filter (pandas query), unique (distinct + counts), groupby, pivot, join.

expr.description: pandas query expression for filter op

web_interact.description: Full interactive Playwright browser control for multi-step automation. Drives real Chromium. RECOMMENDED WORKFLOW for unknown pages: (1) navigate, (2) wait_load for JS-heavy/SPA sites, (3) dismiss_overlays to clear cookie banners/popups/age-gates, (4) get_interactive to see ALL inputs/buttons/links on page with selectors, (5) smart_fill/smart_click using visible text — no CSS selector knowledge required. Also supports: classic click/fill/select with CSS selectors, session persistence, screenshot, evaluate JS, CAPTCHA solving via 2captcha. Call in multiple rounds: navigate+inspect first, then act on what you found.

actions.description: List of action dicts, each with 'type' field. Navigation: navigate(url, wait?), go_back, go_forward, reload. Waiting: wait_selector(selector), wait_url(url_contains), wait_text(text), wait_ms(ms), wait_load() — waits for networkidle, use on JS/React/Next pages. Overlays: dismiss_overlays() — clears cookie banners, GDPR walls, age gates, notification popups (30+ CMP patterns). Introspection: get_interactive([selector]) — returns all inputs/buttons/links with text, type, name, placeholder, selector — USE THIS to understand page structure before acting. Classic: click(selector), type(selector,text), fill(selector,value), fill_form(fields:{}), select(selector,value/label), hover, focus, press(key). Smart: smart_click(text,[role],[exact]) — click by visible text, smart_fill(label,value) — fill input by label/placeholder text, smart_find(text,[role]) — locate element by text. Info: get_text(selector), get_html([selector]), get_url, get_cookies, screenshot([path],[full_page]), evaluate(expression). Cookies: set_cookies, clear_cookies. CAPTCHA: check_captcha, solve_captcha(api_key,[sitekey],[page_url]).

session_id.description: Session ID for cookie persistence across calls

timeout_ms.description: Default timeout per action in ms

captcha_api_key.description: 2captcha.com API key for automatic CAPTCHA solving

click_cookie.description: Auto-dismiss cookie consent on page load (30+ CMP patterns)

port_scan.description: TCP port scanner with service detection and banner grabbing. Scans ports concurrently using connect-based technique. Detects 80+ common services (SSH, HTTP, MySQL, Redis, MongoDB, RDP, etc.) from port numbers and banner responses. Use only on systems you own or have written authorization to test.

host.description: Hostname or IP address to scan

grab_banners.description: Try to read service banners for version detection

dir_fuzz.description: HTTP directory and endpoint fuzzer. Brute-forces paths on a web server with concurrent requests using built-in wordlists (common, api, php, asp) or custom wordlist files. Reports interesting responses by status code. Supports extension fuzzing (try each path with .php, .bak, etc.) and basic recursive scanning. Use only on systems you own or have written authorization to test.

wordlist.description: Built-in wordlist: 'common', 'api', 'php', 'asp' — or absolute path to a custom wordlist file

dns_recon.description: DNS reconnaissance and subdomain enumeration. Queries all common record types (A, AAAA, MX, NS, TXT, CNAME, SOA, SRV), attempts zone transfers (AXFR), brute-forces subdomains with a 100+ word built-in list, and queries crt.sh certificate transparency logs for additional subdomains. Use only on domains you own or have written authorization to test.

record_types.description: DNS record types to query (default: all common types)

zone_transfer.description: Attempt AXFR zone transfer from nameservers

web_audit.description: Comprehensive web security auditor. Checks: missing/misconfigured security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, etc.), cookie security attributes (Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite), CORS misconfigurations (wildcard, credentialed), dangerous HTTP methods (TRACE/PUT/DELETE), open redirect vulnerabilities, information leakage (stack traces, version headers, exposed files), technology fingerprinting (CMS/framework/server/WAF), and robots.txt sensitive path disclosure. Returns findings sorted by severity. Use only on systems you own or have written authorization to test.

sqli_test.description: SQL injection vulnerability tester. Tests URL parameters for error-based (detects DB error strings from MySQL/PostgreSQL/MSSQL/Oracle/SQLite), boolean-based blind (response comparison with true/false conditions), and time-based blind (SLEEP/WAITFOR delays) SQL injection. Auto-detects parameters from URL query string. Read-only probes — does not write to or delete from databases. Use only on systems you own or have written authorization to test.

url.description: Target URL with query parameters (e.g. https://example.com/search?q=test)

params.description: Specific parameter names to test (auto-detects from URL if empty)

ssl_inspect.description: SSL/TLS certificate and configuration inspector. Extracts: certificate details (issuer, subject, SANs, expiry, serial), protocol version support (SSLv2/3, TLS 1.0/1.1/1.2/1.3), active cipher suite, and vulnerability indicators (DROWN, POODLE, BEAST, deprecated protocols, weak ciphers, expired/self-signed/hostname-mismatched certs). Uses Python ssl + openssl CLI for protocol probing.

tech_detect.description: Technology fingerprinting for web targets. Identifies: web servers (Apache/Nginx/IIS/Caddy), CDN/WAF (Cloudflare/Akamai/Fastly/Sucuri/Incapsula), backend language/runtime (PHP/ASP.NET/Node/Python), CMS (WordPress/Drupal/Joomla/Magento/Shopify), frontend frameworks (React/Next.js/Angular/Vue), JavaScript libraries (jQuery/Bootstrap/Tailwind), analytics (GA/GTM/Mixpanel/HotJar), payment providers (Stripe/PayPal), and security tools (reCAPTCHA/hCaptcha). Also fetches IP geolocation, ASN, and hosting organization via ipinfo.io.

include_ip_info.description: Fetch IP geolocation and ASN info

propose_style_questions.description: Presents a visual style questionnaire to the user BEFORE writing any frontend/UI code. Call this when building or redesigning any UI and the user has not provided a complete visual specification. Pass 2-4 targeted questions, each covering a different visual dimension, each with exactly 3 meaningfully-different options. After calling this tool, write one brief acknowledgment sentence and STOP — do not write any HTML, CSS, or JavaScript until the user answers.

questions.description: Array of 2-4 style questions. Each question must cover a distinct visual dimension (background, color palette, typography, layout density, border style, etc.). Do not ask two questions about the same aspect.

question.description: Short, concrete question about one visual design dimension

options.description: Exactly 3 meaningfully different options — specific and descriptive, not vague adjectives like light/medium/dark

discord_tool.description:
Full Discord REST API client operating as the authenticated user (self-bot / user-token mode). The user has explicitly connected their Discord account in Settings and consented to AI-driven automation. You act AS the user — messages you send appear to come from their account, guilds you create belong to them, etc.

REQUIREMENT: If the user has not connected Discord yet, tell them to go to Settings → Discord and click 'Connect Discord'. The tool will return an error if not connected.

PARAMETER: Every call requires 'action' (string). Additional parameters depend on the action.

IDs: Discord uses Snowflake IDs (large integers as strings). When the user says 'in #general', use list_channels first to resolve channel names to IDs. Always prefer IDs over names when you have them cached.

═══════════════════════════════
ACCOUNT & PROFILE
═══════════════════════════════

get_me — Returns own profile: id, username, global_name, discriminator, email, avatar, flags, premium_type. No params.

edit_me — Edit own profile. Optional: username, global_name (display name), bio, avatar ('data:image/png;base64,...'), banner, accent_color (int RGB).

set_status — Set presence + custom status. Optional: status ('online'|'idle'|'dnd'|'invisible'), custom_text, custom_emoji (unicode emoji), expires_at (ISO8601 or null).
  Example: discord_tool(action='set_status', status='dnd', custom_text='In a meeting', custom_emoji='📵')

get_settings — Returns Discord client settings (theme, locale, notification prefs).

get_connections — Returns linked Twitch, Spotify, Steam, GitHub, etc. accounts.

get_nitro_info — Returns active Nitro subscription info.

═══════════════════════════════
GUILDS / SERVERS
═══════════════════════════════

list_guilds — All guilds the user is in. Each has id, name, icon, owner, permissions, features. Optional: with_details (bool) for full per-guild fetch.

get_guild — Full details including member counts, channels, roles, features, owner_id, verification_level. Required: guild_id.

create_guild — Create a new server. Required: name. Optional: icon (data URI), verification_level (0-4), default_message_notifications (0=all/1=mentions), explicit_content_filter (0-2).

edit_guild — Modify guild (requires MANAGE_GUILD). Required: guild_id. Optional: name, icon, banner, splash, description, preferred_locale, verification_level, default_message_notifications, afk_timeout (60/300/900/1800/3600), afk_channel_id, system_channel_id.

leave_guild — Leave a server (cannot be owner). Required: guild_id.

delete_guild — Permanently delete a guild (must be owner). IRREVERSIBLE. Required: guild_id.

get_guild_preview — Public preview of any guild even if not a member. Required: guild_id.

get_guild_vanity_url — Get vanity invite code for guilds that have one. Required: guild_id.

═══════════════════════════════
CHANNELS
═══════════════════════════════
Channel types: 0=text, 2=voice, 4=category, 5=announcement, 10/11/12=threads, 13=stage, 15=forum.

list_channels — All channels in guild. Required: guild_id. Optional: type (int) to filter.

get_channel — Full channel details. Required: channel_id.

create_channel — Create channel (requires MANAGE_CHANNELS). Required: guild_id, name. Optional: type (int, default 0=text), topic (max 1024 chars), category_id, position, nsfw, rate_limit_per_user (0-21600s), bitrate, user_limit.

edit_channel — Modify channel. Required: channel_id. Optional: name, topic, position, nsfw, rate_limit_per_user, bitrate, user_limit, category_id.

delete_channel — Delete a channel. Required: channel_id.

get_channel_permissions — Returns permission_overwrites array. Required: channel_id.

═══════════════════════════════
MESSAGES
═══════════════════════════════

get_messages — Message history (newest first by default). Required: channel_id. Optional: limit (1-100, default 50), before/after/around (message Snowflake IDs).

get_message — Single message. Required: channel_id, message_id.

send_message — Send to any accessible channel or DM. Required: channel_id. Optional: content (up to 2000 chars), embeds (array), tts (bool), reply_to (message Snowflake), allowed_mentions. Must have content or embeds.
  Embed fields: title, description, url, color (int), fields [{name,value,inline}], author {name,url,icon_url}, footer {text,icon_url}, image {url}, thumbnail {url}.
  Example: discord_tool(action='send_message', channel_id='456', content='Hello!', embeds=[{'title':'Alert','color':16711680}])

send_reply — Reply to a specific message with quote. Required: channel_id, message_id, content.

edit_message — Edit own message. Required: channel_id, message_id. Optional: content, embeds.

delete_message — Delete a message. Required: channel_id, message_id.

bulk_delete_messages — Delete up to 10 messages sequentially. Required: channel_id, message_ids (array of strings).

pin_message / unpin_message — Pin/unpin. Required: channel_id, message_id.

get_pinned_messages — All pinned messages. Required: channel_id.

search_messages — Search in guild or channel. Required: query, and guild_id OR channel_id. Optional: author_id, mentions, has ('link'|'embed'|'file'|'video'|'image'|'sound'|'sticker'), before/after (Snowflake), limit (max 25).

start_typing — Show typing indicator for ~5s. Required: channel_id.

═══════════════════════════════
REACTIONS
═══════════════════════════════

add_reaction — Add emoji reaction. Required: channel_id, message_id, emoji (unicode '👍' or 'name:id' for custom).

remove_reaction — Remove own reaction. Required: channel_id, message_id, emoji. Optional: user_id (default @me).

get_reactions — Who reacted with an emoji. Required: channel_id, message_id, emoji. Optional: limit (1-100).

clear_reactions — Remove ALL reactions (requires MANAGE_MESSAGES). Required: channel_id, message_id.

═══════════════════════════════
THREADS
═══════════════════════════════

create_thread — Required: channel_id, name. Optional: message_id (attach to message), auto_archive_duration (60/1440/4320/10080 min), type (11=public/12=private), rate_limit_per_user.

list_threads — Active threads in guild. Required: guild_id.

join_thread / leave_thread — Join or leave a thread. Required: channel_id.

═══════════════════════════════
MEMBERS & MODERATION
═══════════════════════════════

list_guild_members — Required: guild_id. Optional: limit (1-1000), after (Snowflake).

search_guild_members — Search by username/nick prefix. Required: guild_id, query. Optional: limit.

get_member — Member's guild profile. Required: guild_id, user_id.

edit_member — Requires MANAGE_MEMBERS/ROLES/MUTE perms depending on fields changed. Required: guild_id, user_id. Optional: nick (string|null), roles (FULL list of role IDs — replaces all), mute (bool), deaf (bool), communication_disabled_until (ISO8601|null).
  IMPORTANT: 'roles' replaces ALL roles — fetch current roles first when adding just one.

edit_own_nick — Change own nickname. Required: guild_id, nick.

kick_member — Remove from guild. Required: guild_id, user_id.

ban_member — Ban permanently. Required: guild_id, user_id. Optional: delete_message_seconds (0-604800).

unban_member — Remove ban. Required: guild_id, user_id.

list_bans — All bans in guild. Required: guild_id. Optional: limit, after.

timeout_member — Mute across all channels until timestamp. Required: guild_id, user_id, until (ISO8601 or null to remove).

═══════════════════════════════
ROLES
═══════════════════════════════

list_roles — All roles sorted by position (highest = most powerful). Required: guild_id.

create_role — Required: guild_id. Optional: name, permissions (bit string), color (int RGB: 16711680=red, 65280=green, 255=blue, 0=no color), hoist (bool, show separately), mentionable (bool).

edit_role — Required: guild_id, role_id. Optional: name, permissions (string), color (int), hoist, mentionable, position.

delete_role — Required: guild_id, role_id.

add_role_to_member — Required: guild_id, user_id, role_id.

remove_role_from_member — Required: guild_id, user_id, role_id.

═══════════════════════════════
INVITES
═══════════════════════════════

create_invite — Required: channel_id (use a text channel). Optional: max_age (secs, 0=permanent, default 86400), max_uses (0=unlimited), temporary (bool), unique (bool). Returns object with 'url' field = full discord.gg link.

list_invites — Required: guild_id.

get_invite — Lookup any invite. Required: code (the part after discord.gg/).

delete_invite — Revoke invite. Required: code.

═══════════════════════════════
DIRECT MESSAGES
═══════════════════════════════

get_dm_channels — All open DM channels.

create_dm — Open DM with user. Required: user_id. Returns channel object.

send_dm — Send DM, opens channel automatically. Required: user_id, content. Optional: embeds.

close_dm — Remove from sidebar. Required: channel_id.

═══════════════════════════════
FRIENDS & RELATIONSHIPS
═══════════════════════════════

get_relationships — All relationships. Optional: type (1=friends, 2=blocked, 3=incoming, 4=outgoing).

send_friend_request — Required: username ('User' or 'User#1234' for legacy).

remove_friend — Required: user_id.

block_user / unblock_user — Required: user_id.

═══════════════════════════════
USER LOOKUP
═══════════════════════════════

get_user — Basic public profile. Required: user_id.

get_user_profile — Detailed profile + mutual guilds/friends. Required: user_id. Optional: guild_id.

═══════════════════════════════
WEBHOOKS
═══════════════════════════════

get_guild_webhooks / get_channel_webhooks — Required: guild_id or channel_id.

Find guild by name: list_guilds → match name → extract id
Find channel by name: list_channels(guild_id) → match name → extract id
Find user in guild: search_guild_members(guild_id, query=name) → extract user.id

scheduler_tool.description:
Start an autonomous long-running background task that runs for a set duration, uses tools (Discord, web, memory, etc.), and posts a full report back to the chat when finished. A live countdown timer with current status is shown in the UI during execution.

USE CASES:
- 'Chat with @user on Discord for 30 minutes in my name'
- 'Monitor channel #general for 1 hour and respond to messages mentioning me'
- 'Every 2 minutes, check if new PRs appeared on repo X and track them'
- 'Spend 20 minutes researching topic Y and compile notes'

PARAMETERS:
  task (str, REQUIRED): Plain-language description of the full task. Be specific — include channel IDs, usernames, goals, rules, and any constraints. The worker AI reads this as its primary instruction.

  duration_min (int, default 30): Minutes to run. Range: 1–480. The task WILL end at this time regardless of completion.

  wake_every_sec (int, default 90): Seconds between wake cycles. Each cycle: worker reads context, calls tools, takes action. Lower = more responsive, more API cost. Recommended: 60 for active chat, 120 for monitoring, 300 for research.

  label (str, optional): Short title shown in the chat timer bubble. Default: first 80 chars of task.

  context (str, optional): Extra context appended to worker system prompt — useful for passing current state, IDs, or preferences the worker should know upfront.

WORKFLOW:
1. Call scheduler_tool with the task description.
2. Tool spawns a background worker and returns immediately.
3. Chat shows a live countdown timer bubble with current action and stats.
4. User can continue chatting — the worker runs independently.
5. When done, the report streams into chat as a new assistant message.
6. Timer bubble transitions to 'Complete' state.

IMPORTANT:
- The worker has full tool access: discord_tool, web_search, web_fetch, memory_store, memory_get, run_python, github_ops.
- Discord tasks require the user to have connected their Discord account in Settings.
- The task description should be detailed enough for the worker to operate without asking questions.
- For Discord chat tasks: provide channel_id or DM user_id, not just names.
- Worker maintains action history across cycles — it won't repeat completed actions.
- Cancellable via Settings → Active Tasks (future UI) or by starting a new conversation.

task.description: Full task description. Be specific: include IDs, goals, constraints, rules.

label.description: Short display label for the timer bubble (default: first 80 chars of task)

context.description: Extra context for the worker (current state, IDs, preferences)
